assumptions: One Transfer is one outgoing request and its captured Batch. prepare executes Routing.exportRef with that batch identity; the first-write token guard prevents further preparation after the callback right is transferred. Peer capacity and lifetime admission follow the Routing contract.

The production FnOnce closure owns the concrete Batch. RequestWrite moves the closure out under its mutex; callback invocation or destruction occurs afterwards. commitDue and rollbackDue represent that interval and are incremented only by the actual ownership decision.

Architecture facts/resources use explicit frame rules. Cleanup completion can return only the designated cleanupResource and cleanupOwner, after the corresponding LIFO work is terminal; raw completeCleanup resource events are excluded from the system interface.

The global storage projection erases non-storage events. Recovery uses StorageProgram.actualRecovery and its constructed journal, with backup coverage derived from the initial write-name list. I/O atomicity and durability primitives use the StorageProgram source contract.
The system theorem is for these declared events and handoffs. Full Rust/OS scheduling and object-representation semantics are supplied by the implementation bridges and runtime contracts.
